Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmembers wished everyone happy and safe holidays.

  Councilmember Asatryan announced that the Republic of Artsakh had been landlocked for
  several days and called it a humanitarian crisis because there is no way for the people of
  Artsakh to get medical supplies, food, gas, and utilities at this time. Given that the City of
  Glendale already passed a Resolution in support of Artsakh back in December of 2020,
  Asatryan asked Council to put out a statement joining in solidarity with the people of Artsakh
  and condemning Azerbaijan’s actions in keeping the people of Artsakh landlocked. Brotman
  seconded.

  Councilmember Najarian provided his comments regarding the internal memo Council
  received on the removal of the traffic calming measures placed in Adams Hill. He stated that
  this should be brought to Council for a discussion on why those measures were installed
  and why they are being considered for removal. He indicated that it would be helpful for the
  Council to access what worked and what did not work to make improvements for future
  measures and processes. Asatryan stated that she met with a resident who spoke to her on
  behalf of several residents with language barriers, who had these traffic calming measures
  were installed right in front of their homes. The residents were complaining that these traffic
  calming measures were causing them sleepless nights due to the noise they created. She
  also received similar complaints from other residents via emails. Since Council will not meet
  again until January, Asatryan asked staff to provide a remedy until this item is agenized for
  the January 2023 Council meeting. City Manager Roubik Golanian indicated that these
  traffic calming measures were a pilot program and were not intended to be placed or
  installed on a permanent basis. He stated that the purpose of the pilot program was to
  assess the impacts of these measures on calming traffic while also getting input from the
  community. He also reiterated that there will be an opportunity for staff and the Council to
  reassess these measures.

  Mayor Kassakhian urged residents to be careful while driving during the holidays, as there
  are many distracted drivers, and to be kind to one another. He also asked the public to take
  precautions regarding package deliveries to their homes because there is often an uptick in

  3
   the rate of mail and package thefts during this time of year. Mayor Kassakhian thanked his
  colleagues and Mayor Pro Tem, Dan Brotman, for running the meetings while he was
  out last week as he was recovering from a fall. He thanked the kind individuals who stopped
  to make sure he was okay. Kassakhian asked staff to provide a status on the Rockhaven
  Sanitarium after the recent inclement weather. Kassakhian said he received emails from the
  public regarding the condition of the building and asked whether staff can comment about
  what is being done to prevent the building from further deterioration. Director of Public
  Works Yazdan Emrani stated that the city advertised for bids to replace the roofs, place
  tarps and also remedy some of hazardous materials. The bids they received for the
  remediation of hazardous materials were reasonable. However, the bids on the other two
  items that they received were a bit excessive. The city followed up with the contractor to find
  out why the price was so high, and the contractor stated that it was due to the historic nature
  of the buildings and the amount of work that it would take to mitigate the issues. Emrani
  stated that the Department of Public Works is asking to go out for new bids and they would
  like to have separate bids for the different projects - one for the removal of hazardous
  materials and the other for the roofing and the tarps. Kassakhian asked if something could
  be done soon since the project is already delayed, and the wet season is already here.

  Kassakhian thanked Stephen Meek for bringing up the issue of paving certain streets. He
  asked staff to provide a report on when the streets were last redone and paved and have
  that information for public viewing on the city website. Kassakhian attended several events
  including Glendale Arts Open House Holiday event, Salvation Army’s Kettle Kickoff, and the
  Glendale Rotary Noon’s 100th Anniversary.
